chunks: And with the first chain of narration from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ibn Mahboob, from al-Fadhl ibn Yunus, from Abu al-Hasan the First, peace be upon him, that he said:

Convey good, and speak good, and do not be an Imma’ah. I said: What is an Imma’ah? He said: Do not say 'I am with the people and I am just like anyone of them.' Surely, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: O people, there are but two paths: the path of good and the path of evil. So why is it that the path of evil is more beloved to you than the path of good?!
And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah bless our master Muhammad and his pure progeny and grant them abundant peace.

key_terms.إِمَّعَة: Imma’ah: a person who blindly follows the crowd without independent thought, a yes-man or conformist
key_terms.نَجْد: Najd: path, road, or way — used here in the sense of a moral path or direction in life

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Kadhim (AS) mean by Imma’ah and why does Islam warn against blind conformism?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of al-Shaykh al-Mufid, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) commands the narrator to convey and speak good, and strictly warns against being an Imma’ah — a person who blindly conforms to whatever others do without independent moral judgment. When asked to clarify, the Imam explains that an Imma’ah says 'I am with the people; I am just like anyone else,' and then cites the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) who questioned why people are more drawn to the path of evil than the path of good. This teaching was directed at the Shia community during a time when conformism with oppressive authorities was a significant moral challenge.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 47. And with the foregoing chains of narration from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ibn Mahboob, from al-Fadhl ibn Yunus, from: Abul Hasan, the first, peace be upon him said:

"Convey that which is good, and speak that which is good and do not be Imma’ah! I said: "What is Imma’ah?" He said: "Do not have a habit of saying: I am from the people and I am just like any one of them. Surely, the messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his progeny, said: O people, there are but two paths: path of good and path of evil. What is the matter with you that I find the path of evil is more loved by you than the path of good?"
Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds and may Allah bless our master, Muhammad and his pure progeny, and salutations upon them.
